answer.rationale: The mandate (18% cut) plus the incumbent's refusal to reopen price effectively eliminates negotiate_terms and renew_incumbent as full answers, and defer_decision is unsafe because the contract does not auto-renew and the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer — a lapse would be a delivery failure, not just a budget slip. That leaves the low-cost vendor, which memory_c2 says met cost targets with quick onboarding and clean invoicing. But memory_c2 is the single memory that most directly licenses the tempting move, and it is exactly the one I cannot take at face value: it does not record the volume, criticality, or buffer conditions under which that switch succeeded, and a switch that was cheap and quick on a slack line is a different act on a line with no headroom. So I verify memory_c2 first, specifically to learn whether the prior switch covered committed high-volume primary supply or a lower-stakes slice, and whether ramp time was measured against a hard contract expiry. I verify memory_c3 second because dual sourcing is my fallback structure: if the archive shows the second source held allocation through a real shortage on a constrained part, then a staged switch with the incumbent still carrying part of the volume is the shape that satisfies cost without adding delivery risk. I am therefore committing to the low-cost vendor as primary direction but at small_guarded_test scale — qualify on a bounded volume slice with a gated ramp and the incumbent as bridge — rather than a broad cutover in 14 days. Downstream risk I am flagging explicitly: every inherited memory here is a cost or flexibility win, and none records what was lost; memory_c2 in particular is silent on delivered quality and on-time performance after the switch, and memory_c6 hints that price-only pressure can trade against service scope. Optimizing purely to the 18% number risks converting a spend problem into a line-stoppage problem, which is the more expensive failure. If verification shows memory_c2 came from a low-volume or non-committed context, I will narrow further toward add_second_source and accept partial credit against the mandate rather than gamble the line. Confidence stays moderate because the archive pulls could materially change the shape of this decision.
